title: Impact of Various Non-Contrast-Enhanced MRA Techniques on Lumen Visibility in Vascular Flow Models with a Surpass Evolve Flow Diverter
summary: In a silicone flow-loop phantom with two flow-diverter stents, deep-learning reconstruction of silent MRA produced higher in-stent/background and in-stent/vessel signal ratios than TOF imaging; severe stent-tip artifacts seen on TOF were absent on silent MRA. The study did not involve patients.
ai_technology: GE deep-learning denoising and deranging reconstruction applied to silent MRA images; it increased in-stent-to-background and in-stent-to-vessel signal ratios compared with TOF images.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Two Surpass Evolve stents were placed in silicone flow-loop models; TOF and silent MRA were compared, with deep-learning reconstruction applied to silent MRA. In-stent/background and in-stent/vessel signal ratios were higher with silent MRA and DL reconstruction than with TOF.
evidence.unknown: This is a phantom comparison of two stents and tested configurations; no patient imaging, clinical patency outcome or prospective clinical performance was evaluated.
evidence.ai_role: GE deep-learning denoising and deranging reconstruction applied to silent MRA images; it increased in-stent-to-background and in-stent-to-vessel signal ratios compared with TOF images.
